Oral health is a fundamental component of overall health and well-being, directly impacting an individual’s quality of life
. As the healthcare industry continues to modernize, the adoption of specialized health information technology has become essential for clinical efficiency and improved patient care
. Dental Information Management Systems have emerged to help transition clinics from traditional to streamlined digital environments

. These systems facilitate the secure management of Electronic Medical Records (EMR), patient history, inventory, and scheduling, thereby reducing administrative burdens and allowing dental practitioners to focus primarily on patient treatment
Despite growing technology and digitalization, many startup and expanding dental clinics still rely on manual methods for their daily operations
. This often results in disorganized patient records, scheduling conflicts, and inefficient clinic management
. Furthermore, patients frequently experience anxiety or hesitation due to a lack of accessible, personalized dental health information

. Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) for educational patient engagement and predictive scheduling addresses this gap, providing patients with a clearer understanding of their oral health and fostering higher trust and satisfaction

To address these operational and patient engagement challenges is a highly necessary and impactful step for growing dental practices. Developing an integrated platform that automates clinic workflows such as centralizing electronic medical records (EMR), modernized appointment scheduling, and utilizing artificial intelligence for patient education and predictive scheduling, can significantly resolve existing operational problems. Various studies provided evidence that the implementation of specialized information systems across different medical and dental clinics has greatly improved overall clinical efficiency
, and elevated the quality of patient care
. Therefore, applying these technological innovations is important in bridging the gap between traditional manual operations and modernized dental healthcare delivery.

To fulfill this objective globally, the healthcare industry is actively transitioning from traditional practices to digital health information systems to improve patient outcomes and clinic operations

This chapter provides an overview of previous research, literature, and existing systems related to dental information management, artificial intelligence in healthcare, and patient engagement. It introduces the framework and justification for the development of the proposed system, highlighting the features that distinguish it from currently available applications.
History of Dental Clinics in the Philippines
The historical evolution of dental clinics in the Philippines represents a gradual shift from traditional, hands-on physical methods to the modern integration of advanced technologies
. In recent years, a major focus has been placed on how dental education shapes the clinic of the future

. A 2025 comparative study highlighted that while other Asian nations have rapidly embedded computer-based methods into their national teaching plans, the integration of digital technologies in Philippine dental technician education remains in its early, basic stages
. This historical transition period highlights a critical gap where conventional practical training must be updated to meet the evolving demands of modern, technology-driven dental clinics

Furthermore, the demographic and generational profile of the professionals operating these clinics has evolved significantly. Over the past few decades, the personality traits and working styles of dental students have shifted, which directly impacts clinic management and patient interaction. A 2024 detailed review and data comparison of dental students globally revealed that the dominant personality profiles of dental students in the Philippines uniquely differ from those in the United States or other Asian countries

. This evolution in practitioner backgrounds suggests that modern Philippine dental clinics are fostering highly distinct, culturally specific approaches to patient care and inter-office communication compared to earlier generations.

Finally, the recent history of Philippine dental care has been marked by a necessary evolution toward public health integration and awareness of elderly care. As the population ages, historical models of treating only sudden, severe pain are no longer sufficient. A recent

2026 study across multiple locations validated the Ageism Scale for Dental Students across several Asian countries, including the Philippines, marking a new era in educational history where multicultural and elderly care skills are actively measured and taught
. This modern evolution ensures that the next generation of dental clinics will be better equipped to handle the complex, long-term oral health needs of an aging demographic.

Taking care of your mouth provides profound benefits that extend far beyond preventing cavities; it is a foundational pillar for maintaining a balanced biological ecosystem. Modern dental science heavily emphasizes the benefits of managing the mouth's natural bacteria to prevent imbalance, which causes severe conditions like advanced gum disease
. A 2026 systematic review demonstrated that introducing treatments using helpful bacteria, such as
, can significantly reduce cavity-causing bacteria amounts in the saliva

. By actively managing this bacterial environment, individuals can experience measurable improvements in gum health, proving that daily oral care is an active defense mechanism against long-lasting oral infections.
Beyond the mouth, the whole-body benefits of rigorous oral care are undeniable, particularly regarding long-term disease prevention

. Maintaining a consistent oral hygiene routine actively reduces the burden of widespread body swelling that can travel through the bloodstream. A comprehensive 2026 detailed data review confirmed a two-way relationship over time between advanced gum disease and whole-body conditions affecting energy use; specifically, individuals suffering from advanced gum disease were found to have a 19–26% higher occurrence of newly incident type 2 diabetes during follow-up
. Proper oral care mitigates these risks, serving as a critical preventive measure that protects
and heart health over a person's lifetime.

The benefits of oral care are also heavily amplified when combined with proper nutrition. Recent literature highlights the significant advantage of incorporating functional and organic foods to enhance dental hygiene. A comprehensive 2026 review illustrated that healthy natural chemicals found in certain fruits, vegetables, and probiotics possess antioxidant properties that combat the cell damage associated with oral diseases
. By integrating these functional nutrients into a daily diet, patients can naturally lower their risk
for root canal infections, mouth tissue swelling, and severe bad breath, thereby achieving a holistic benefit that encompasses both dietary and dental health.
Current State of Dental Care Delivery in the Philippines
The current state of dental care delivery in the Philippines is heavily influenced by a massive national burden of oral diseases
. According to a 2026 analysis of the Global Burden of Disease across ASEAN member states, oral disorders account for nearly half of all-cause prevalence in the region

. In the Philippines, this burden is driven primarily by untreated cavities of permanent teeth and widespread gum disease, which continue to rise due to population growth and aging demographics. Despite modern advancements in care, demographic pressures currently outpace the reach of preventive dental delivery, highlighting a critical gap in regional health planning.

Within clinical settings, the delivery of dental care has become increasingly complex due to the rising rate of other existing health conditions among Filipino patients. Dentists are no longer just treating teeth; they are managing complex medical profiles at the dental chair. A 2026 study reviewing past data conducted at a Philippine university dental clinic revealed that local gum disease patients present with significantly higher rates of high blood pressure and heart diseases compared to non-gum disease patients
. This current reality requires modern Philippine dental care delivery systems to seamlessly integrate basic medical screening
, such as blood pressure monitoring and diabetic risk assessment, into routine gum health consultations

To combat these overlapping clinical and socioeconomic challenges, the public health sector is currently exploring ways to broaden care delivery through national insurance frameworks. Because non-hospital dental services have historically relied heavily on out-of-pocket payments, lower-income populations often delay treatment until emergencies arise
. Recently, the government has been actively analyzing the cost-effectiveness of integrating a comprehensive oral health care package into the PhilHealth benefit system
. This proposed transition aims to shift the current delivery model from reactive, emergency-based extractions toward accessible, subsidized primary preventive care for all Filipinos.
Common Operational Challenges in Dental Clinics

Operating a modern dental clinic involves navigating a complex web of logistical, financial, and patient-management hurdles. One of the most persistent operational challenges stems from the lasting impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. While a recent 2025 study confirmed that standard, high-level precautions effectively prevented the spread of the virus within dental settings
, the financial and temporal burden of maintaining these strict rules for procedures that spray liquids into the air remains

. Clinics continue to face the operational challenge of balancing heightened costs for advanced personal protective equipment and extended room-turnover times with the need to maintain a profitable daily patient volume

Another major management hurdle is aligning the clinic's operational performance with patient expectations. Evaluating service quality is critical for a clinic's survival, yet many practices struggle with administrative inefficiencies
. A recent 2024 method of measuring service importance versus performance of dental clinics identified a significant operational gap in areas categorized as "responsiveness" and "reliability"

. This indicates that while clinical treatments may be adequate, clinic managers face immense challenges in ensuring that front-desk staff are highly accountable, appointments run exactly on time, and patient communications are handled efficiently without causing frustration.

Furthermore, integrating new digital technologies poses a steep operational barrier for many developing or smaller clinics. As the industry pushes toward digital transformation, clinics must manage the transition from paper to electronic systems. A 2024 study assessing the implementation of digital patient files in developing settings highlighted severe organizational challenges, including a lack of necessary standards for data exchange, legal privacy concerns, and the high financial cost of constantly training staff
. Overcoming staff resistance to new workflows while managing these technological investments is a daily challenge for modern clinic owners.

A Dental Information Management System (DIMS), commonly referred to as an Electronic Medical Record (EMR), is designed to replace traditional paper charts and centralize all clinical data [34]. The primary advantage of these systems is their ability to

securely store vast amounts of historical diagnostic data, moving beyond basic charting to support broader public health initiatives. In fact, a 2021 dental record-based surveillance study proved that these digital files can be actively mined to monitor non-communicable health conditions across thousands of patients seamlessly [35]. By utilizing an electronic infrastructure, clinics transform static paperwork into dynamic, searchable databases.
The administrative and clinical workflows of dental practice are heavily optimized through the ability to share information smoothly within modern DIMS
. One of the greatest risks in dentistry is treating a patient without full knowledge of their medical background. A 2026 qualitative study highlighted that integrating the E
directly with broader national medical databases allows dental practitioners instant access to crucial medication information and laboratory values

. This seamless sharing of information resolves major documentation bottlenecks, reduces the risk of adverse drug interactions during procedures, and ensures a much safer, coordinated approach to patient care.

Beyond daily organization, the true future of Dental Information Management Systems lies in using data to predict future health conditions. With thousands of fully digitized patient files available, Patel et al. (2022) demonstrated how machine learning models can be applied directly to electronic dental records to predict periodontal disease

Recent pilot studies have utilized advanced computer programs that learn from data on comprehensive EMR data to successfully predict a patient's risk for severe periodontitis progression, and even flag potential risks of brain and nerve diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease based on oral health markers
This marks a revolutionary shift where DIMS not only manage the clinic schedule but actively assist the dentist in predicting and preventing severe diseases before they occur.
Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) and Data Security
The transition to Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) has dramatically improved healthcare efficiency, but it has simultaneously introduced severe vulnerabilities regarding data security

. A major contemporary issue is the rapid grouping together of the EMR market, where most medical institutions now rely on a highly concentrated number of software vendors and shared cloud hosting platforms. A 2025 analysis highlighted that this structural consolidation creates a dangerous one weak spot that could break the whole system within the healthcare system. A single successful cyberattack or breach on a primary
vendor could instantly expose millions of sensitive patient files while crippling clinical care and billing operations across thousands of hospitals globally
. Consequently, health policy experts are increasingly advocating for robust governmental oversight and stricter vendor security mandates to mitigate these catastrophic risks to the entire system

When these centralized systems fail, the consequences extend far beyond technical disruptions, directly threatening patient safety and clinical ethics. Because modern EMRs store deeply sensitive information ranging from psychiatric notes to reproductive health

unauthorized access can lead to severe psychological, social, and clinical harm for the patient. A 2025 study evaluating the digital transformation of specialized remote healthcare and reproductive care emphasized that cybersecurity is no longer merely an IT concern, but an absolute ethical imperative

. The study argues that failing to secure electronic health records actively violates the principles of patient confidentiality, ultimately degrading the overall quality of care and eroding the foundational trust between patients and the medical community.

To combat these evolving threats, system architects are aggressively developing next-generation security frameworks that move away from traditional centralized databases. The EMR-Chain framework introduced in recent literature demonstrates the successful implementation of decentralized EMR management systems utilizing blockchain technology where data is securely spread across a distributed network of computers

The planning phase serves as the fundamental strategic layer of the software development life cycle, primarily focused on establishing a clear project scope and identifying the core objectives of the system. This stage involves a multidimensional analysis of the organizational environment, the identification of key stakeholders, and the rigorous assessment of resource limitations and potential risks
. This phase must produce a baseline project plan that defines the schedule, technical requirements, and budget constraints to prevent "scope creep" during later stages of the development cycle

. Furthermore, a feasibility study is conducted during this phase to evaluate whether the proposed solution is technically, economically, and operationally viable within the project's specific context
. By creating a structured roadmap, the project team ensures that the development process remains aligned with the strategic goals of the client throughout the entire lifecycle.

The researchers initiated the process by conducting formal meetings and Onsite and On-call Interviews with Dr. Michael Edwin Tamayo and the clinic staff to gain a comprehensive understanding of manual processes and operational pain points. Through these sessions and the distribution of Google Forms, the team identified specific opportunities for improvement in appointment scheduling, patient records management, and inventory tracking. Finally, the team assessed critical environmental challenges, including the varying levels of digital literacy among clinic staff, internet connectivity reliability, and stringent data privacy requirements for medical records, ensuring the project's long-term sustainability and compliance.

The design phase is a refined modeling stage where abstract requirements are transformed into detailed technical specifications and interactive visual interfaces. This process encompasses the definition of the system architecture, data structures, and the refinement of User Interface (UI) and User Experience (UX) principles to ensure the system is both functional and accessible

. Effective design must prioritize the human-computer interface, ensuring that the system's input and output logic is intuitive for the intended end-users while serving as a bridge between conceptual ideas and executable code
. This phase is often divided into high-level design, which maps out the overall system structure, and low-level design, which specifies the internal logic of individual modules and database schemas

During this phase, the team focused on translating user requirements into concrete visual interfaces before any coding began. Simple and user-friendly screens were designed for all user types, patients accessing the system through the mobile application, and dentists, secretaries, and the clinic owners accessing the system through the web application. Figma and Canva served as the primary design tools for creating wireframes, UI/UX prototypes, and interactive mockups, allowing the team to simulate how the system would look and function in practice. The application's branding, including the logo, color palette, and typography, was finalized during this phase. System diagrams were created to show how the different modules interconnect, such as the flow from the AI Patient Care Companion to the live chat escalation handled by the clinic secretary on the web system. The design focused on smooth navigation and fast task completion, ensuring that the interface was intuitive for both tech-savvy and non-tech-savvy users.

The development phase is the core technical implementation stage where the system’s architecture is translated into functional source code using specific programming languages and frameworks. This phase is characterized by iterative coding cycles, software configuration management, and the constant integration of various modules to build a cohesive, scalable, and secure application
. In modern agile frameworks, this stage relies heavily on refactoring and continuous integration to ensure that the code remains clean and adaptable to changing requirements across platform

During the development phase, the team begins building the web and mobile components of

using a modular and iterative approach. Each sprint focused on completing specific user stories. Collaborative coding and regular peer reviews helped maintain quality and consistency across the project. The patient-facing mobile application was built using React Native with Expo, enabling cross-platform compatibility on both Android and iOS devices. The web system, designed for the clinic owner, dentists, and secretary, was developed using React.js to create interactive and dynamic administrative dashboards. Backend development was done using Node.js and Express.js to handle server-side operations and API management. MongoDB served as the primary cloud database, managed through MongoDB Atlas, ensuring secure and scalable storage for Electronic Medical Records (EMR), inventory data, and user credentials. The Resend email service was integrated for transactional emails including account activation links and OTP password reset codes. JWT-based authentication was implemented to enforce role-based access control across all user types.

The Gemini API was integrated to power the AI Patient Care Companion, while Python and OpenCV were used to support objective image-quality assessment within the AI-Assisted Radiograph Review workflow.
Throughout development, modular coding practices and peer reviews were consistently applied to ensure code quality and maintainability.

The testing phase is a rigorous quality assurance procedure designed to systematically identify and resolve defects, ensuring the software performs reliably under a wide variety of conditions. This stage involves the process of executing a program with the intent of finding errors and verifying that the software performs as expected

. Testing is a hierarchical process, moving from individual units to integrated systems to ensure that the final product is free of critical vulnerabilities and logical errors before it moves into the production environment
. Beyond technical functionality, this phase also includes security testing to protect sensitive data and performance testing to ensure the system remains stable under heavy user loads

By conducting thorough security and usability checks, the development team can guarantee a high standard of performance and minimize the risk of failure in the production environment. The testing phase was carried out continuously throughout the development to ensure that every feature was functional, reliable, and user-friendly. Unit testing was conducted after each module had been developed to confirm that individual functions, such as login validation, appointment booking, inventory alerts, and AI Companion responses, worked as intended. Once the modules were integrated, integration testing was performed to ensure smooth communication among the system's components, particularly between the patient mobile application, the web system, the Node.js backend, and the MongoDB database. Functional and system testing evaluated whether the overall application met its specified requirements under realistic conditions. Before proceeding to full UAT, the researchers applied the Jakob Nielsen Usability Form to evaluate the user interface design based on common usability principles. The results from this evaluation were reviewed and discussed during the User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Feedback and test results were used to fix bugs, enhance user interface components, and refine system behavior. The goal of the testing phase was to deliver a secure, efficient, and easy-to-use system that performed reliably across all user roles and scenarios.

The deployment phase marks the critical transition of the software product from a controlled development environment to a live, production-ready state for end-users. This encompasses the final configuration of cloud servers, the migration of operational data, and the setup of monitoring tools to ensure continuous uptime and performance stability
. Successful deployment is considered a process of "Release Management" that ensures the production environment is stable, secure, and capable of handling real-world traffic
. This phase also involves the implementation of automated deployment pipelines and disaster recovery protocols to ensure data integrity during the transition to the live environment

The system’s quality and acceptability were evaluated using a Use Acceptance Test (UAT) form administered via Microsoft Forms. The evaluation criteria were based on the ISO 9126 Software Quality Standard and Jakob Nielsen’s Usability Testing Principles. The form was structured into five main categories: Functionality, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Compliance, and Usability. Respondents evaluated each statement using a 6-point Likert Scale, providing a precise measure of their perceptions of the system’s effectiveness and usability.

: A Dental Information Management System with AI-Driven Patient Engagement for

Dental Clinic was developed as a centralized mobile and web-based platform intended to improve the management of patient records, appointments, clinic resources, and patient engagement. The project addressed the clinic’s reliance on manual and fragmented processes, including paper-based patient records, appointment coordination through Facebook Messenger, schedule monitoring through Google Calendar and spreadsheets, and visual inspection of dental supply levels. These practices required considerable manual effort and created difficulties in maintaining accurate and synchronized information as the clinic expanded its operations.

The system consists of a patient facing mobile application and a role-based web application connected to centralized backend services and a cloud database. The mobile application allows patients to manage appointments, receive notifications, access selected electronic medical records, review dentist-approved radiographs summaries, monitor their
oral health, brows dental education materials, receive predictive visit recommendations, and communicate with
. The web application provides authorized access to Patients, Clinic Secretaires, Dentists, Branch Managers, Clinic Owners, and the System Administrator according
to their assigned roles and permissions.
The web application supports appointment and schedule management, patient registration user account management, electronic medical records, interactive digital
, material usage logging, inventory monitoring, branch transfers, branch analytics, notifications, activity logs, and system administrations functions.

The AI-Assisted Radiograph Review feature provides objective image-quality information and allows dentists to record clinical findings, add annotations, prepare summary drafts, and approve the final summaries made available to patients. Meanwhile, the AI Patient Care Companion integrates
Management, and Predictive Visit to provide general and non-diagnostic oral health guidance.

The system was developed using React Native for mobile applications, ReactJS for the web frontend, Node.js for backend processing, and MongoDB for centralized data storage. The Gemini API was integrated to support AI-assisted patient engagement, while Python and OpenCV were used to support objective image-quality assessment in the radiograph review workflow. Role-based and branch-based access controls were implemented to restrict access to sensitive patient and operational information.

The developed system underwent unit, integration, functional, compatibility, security, performance, and accessibility testing. For the web system, 66 components across 23 modules passed the unit tests, while all 76 role-based integrated components passed the web integration tests. For the mobile application, all 21 components under nine modules passed the unit tests, and all ten integrated components passed the mobile integration tests. Functional testing also produced a 100% pass rate for the 23 unique web modules and nine mobile modules.

The mobile application was found compatible with the selected Android and iOS configurations, while the web system operated properly across Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, Brave, and Opera GX. The assessed web pages received an A+ security-header rating. Web performance testing produced an average score of approximately 80.98, while accessibility testing produced an average score of approximately 97.58. Mobile performance testing recorded an average application load time of 0.63 seconds, an average response time of 1.44 seconds, and an average screen-rendering time of 1.32 seconds. These results indicate that the system’s essential functions operated as intended, although further interface and performance improvements may enhance the overall user experience.

Dental Clinic. The mobile and web applications provide an integrated platform for managing patient information, appointments, treatment records, dental images, inventory, clinic branches, user accounts, and patient-engagement functions.

The first specific objective was achieved through the development of a centralized Electronic Medical Record system containing patient profiles, medical and dental histories, treatment histories, digital

, and radiograph records. Role-based and branch-based access controls were applied to ensure that users could only access records and functions permitted by their responsibilities and operational scope.

The second objective was achieved through the Appointment and Schedule Management modules and the patient-facing appointment functions available through mobile and web applications. These features centralized appointment requests, clinic schedules, status updates, and notifications. The AI Patient Care Companion further supported patient engagement through
, Dental Education, Oral Health Management, and Predictive Visit.

and AI-Assisted Radiograph Review features. Dentists can document tooth conditions, maintain

histories, assess objective radiographic quality information, record clinical findings, add annotations, and prepare dentist-approved summaries. The radiograph review feature operates strictly as a clinical decision-support tool and does not independently diagnose dental conditions.

These features allow authorized personnel to record materials used during treatment, update inventory quantities, monitor stock levels, receive low-stock alerts, and review operational information that may support future branch-expansion decisions.

Based on the testing results and feedback provided by the evaluators, the following recommendations are proposed to improve the usability, accessibility, accuracy, and functionality of

The phone number field should automatically apply or display the +639 Philippine mobile-number format. Input masking and clear validation messages should also be implemented to help patients enter their contact numbers correctly and consistently.

The appointment form should maintain a stable and organized layout while the user is typing or while the on-screen keyboard is displayed. Its responsive behavior should be tested across different screen sizes to prevent fields, buttons, and other interface elements from shifting, resizing incorrectly, or overlapping.

The placeholder option “Select Branch” should be removed when the branch has already been automatically assigned or selected by the system. The selected branch should remain clearly displayed so patients can confirm where the appointment will take place without performing an unnecessary selection.

Asterisks should only appear beside fields that are required. If the Branch and Procedure fields are optional or automatically completed by the system, their required-field indicators should be removed. The development team should also review all forms and make only information essential to the transaction mandatory.
Form fields should not immediately display a red border or error message merely after being clicked or selected. Validation feedback should appear after the user
leaves an incomplete or invalid field or attempts to submit the form. Error messages should clearly identify the problem and explain how it can be corrected.

The Preferred Time field should remain visible and accessible throughout the appointment process. Unavailable time slots should be displayed but disabled and clearly labeled as “Booked” or “Already Booked” instead of disappearing. This will help patients understand why a particular schedule cannot be selected.
Handle Appointment Details When Changing Branches

When a patient changes the selected branch, the system should retain the previously selected appointment time if the same schedule remains available at the new branch. If the time is unavailable, the system should clear the selection and provide a message explaining that another time must be selected. This prevents unexpected data loss while avoiding invalid appointments.
Define and Validate the Patient Age Requirement

The clinic should establish an accepted patient age range or policy. The system should validate the patient’s age or date of birth according to this policy and provide a clear message when the entered value is outside the permitted range. If minors are accepted, the system may also require appropriate guardian information.

The image in the Orthodontic Services section of the Home page may be removed if the section is intended only to summarize the available services. A concise text-based presentation may reduce confusion and make the information easier to understand, particularly for older users.
A dark or dim display mode may be added to the mobile and web applications to improve viewing comfort under low-light conditions and provide users with an additional accessibility preference.

Inventory alerts should be classified according to urgency, such as “Warning” and “Critical.” Appropriate visual indicators and threshold values should be used so clinic personnel can immediately identify which supplies require attention or replenishment.

Incorrect error messages, missing indicators, overlapping interface entries, and inconsistent visual elements should be reviewed and corrected. The system should use consistent labels, colors, field states, and feedback messages across all modules.
Reduce Repetitive Information and Unnecessary Navigation

Duplicate or repetitive information should be removed where it does not provide additional value. Screen flows may also be simplified by reducing unnecessary tabs or steps, allowing users to complete common tasks with fewer interactions.
Maintenance screens should require only the information necessary to perform a search, filter, or query. Optional advanced filters may be placed in an expandable
so users are not required to complete several fields before retrieving information.

The purpose and computation of the Amount Charged, Amount Paid, and Balance fields should be clearly defined. If partial or installment payments are intended as a future function, the system should provide a transaction history, remaining-balance computation, and clear payment-status indicators.
Future versions may include the automatic calculation of applicable discounts, such as those provided to
with disabilities and other qualified patients. The feature should follow clinic policies and applicable regulations and should retain records supporting the applied discount.

Google Maps, GPS, or another mapping service may be integrated to help patients locate the selected clinic branch. The system may provide the branch address, map position, directions, and a link that opens the location in the patient’s preferred navigation application.

The remaining accessibility issues identified during testing should be corrected. Modules with lower performance scores should also be optimized by improving asset loading, reducing unnecessary scripts, minimizing layout shifts, and reviewing slow network requests.

The proponents or future developers should continue collecting feedback from patients, dentists, clinic personnel, and other authorized users. Regular usability reviews will help identify emerging concerns and ensure that system improvements remain aligned with actual clinic workflows.
Maintain Security, Compatibility, and Data Protection

Future developers should regularly update system dependencies, review access permissions, test database backups, monitor audit trails, and repeat compatibility and security assessments whenever significant system changes are introduced. These measures are particularly important because
processes confidential patient and clinical information.
